html:
The oldest surviving book from Japan, a chronicle of myths, legends and early history presented to Empress Genmei in 712. Its title means "Records of Ancient Matters".

The court official Ō no Yasumaro wrote it down from stories recited by Hieda no Are. It begins with the creation of the world and the gods Izanagi and Izanami, who give birth to the islands of Japan. It tells of the sun goddess Amaterasu and her unruly brother Susanoo, and traces the imperial family back to Amaterasu through the legendary first emperor, Jimmu. It ends with Empress Suiko in the early 600s.

The text uses Chinese characters, some for their meaning and some only for their sound, to write Japanese. Eight years later the court finished the Nihon Shoki, a longer history in formal Chinese.

The Kojiki gave the ruling house of Nara Japan a sacred origin. In the 1700s the scholar Motoori Norinaga made it the core text of a revival of Shinto, and it later fed the emperor cult of modern Japan.
sum: The oldest surviving book from Japan, a chronicle of myths, legends and early history presented to Empress Genmei in 712. Its title means "Records of Ancient Matters".
